existing_identity_primitives: None found as production code. Searched fabric/interface.py, fabric/loopback/, fabric/tcp/, PairingStore, LocalKeyStore, AuthorityContext, NodeIdentity, RemoteCapabilityRequest, wire.py, both server scripts, and every pairing/authority test file for peer/identity/principal/actor/node_id/relationship/device/owner/subject/issuer/claim/credential/trust concepts. Two existing fields were specifically considered and REJECTED as substitutes for peer_id (documented directly in fabric/interface.py's own module comments, per Section 4's explicit instruction): NodeIdentity.node_id (a transient, unpersisted, unrevocable transport-routing identifier -- nothing stores, resolves, or revokes it) and AuthorityContext.actor_id (a free-text authority-attribution string with no validation, persistence, or lifecycle). Neither was reused; a genuinely new PeerIdentityStore was constructed.
chosen_peer_identity_contract: PeerIdentityStore (fabric/interface.py): peer_id (opaque, random, non-secret, PEER-<uuid4 hex>), created_at, status (ACTIVE/REVOKED -- two states only, per Section 15's explicit 'do not implement federation/organizational identity/user accounts'), metadata_version (fixed constant '1', a forward-compatibility placeholder). A SEPARATE append-only peer<->relationship binding ledger (peer_relationship_bindings.jsonl) records which relationship_id(s) are currently accepted for a given peer_id -- Section 7's explicit requirement that 'a peer identity must not become trusted merely because it exists.'
peer_id_generation: envelope.validate_mission_id(f'PEER-{uuid.uuid4().hex}') -- identical generation idiom to relationship_id and key_id, not derived from any secret, username, hostname, IP, or mutable device label.
peer_store: Reuses evidence_envelope.envelope's exact JSONL/file-lock/atomic-write discipline (a seventh application of that pattern, after LineageStore, TrajectoryStore, RequestReplayGuard, LocalKeyStore's metadata ledger, PairingStore's metadata ledger, and now PeerIdentityStore's two ledgers). Supports register_peer/revoke_peer/status_of/resolve_active/bind_relationship/unbind_relationship/is_relationship_bound_to_peer; all proven durable across a fresh store instance and a real second OS subprocess.
relationship_binding: bind_relationship(peer_id, relationship_id) appends a BOUND record to the separate bindings ledger; unbind_relationship() appends UNBOUND for that exact pair only (does not affect any other binding either identifier may have). is_relationship_bound_to_peer() checks the LATEST record for the exact pair. Revoking a peer does NOT retroactively unbind its relationships (orthogonal lifecycles, proven by TestRevokedRelationshipZeroExecution/TestRevokedKeyZeroExecution-style composition) -- but resolve_active(peer_id) returning None for a revoked peer means the enforcement gate rejects regardless of any surviving binding record.
request_identity_binding: source_peer_id: Optional[str] = None added to RemoteCapabilityRequest (new optional field, no incompatible migration) and included in canonical_request_fields()'s HMAC-signed content, identically to how relationship_id was added in the parent mission -- mutating source_peer_id after signing invalidates the tag exactly like mutating capability_id or relationship_id would.
actor_id_semantics: AuthorityContext.actor_id was NOT touched and is never read, compared against, or derived from source_peer_id anywhere in this mission's code. TestActorIdRemainsIndependent proves directly: the same peer_id executes successfully alongside a DIFFERENT, unrelated actor_id value, with no cross-check performed. Recorded decision: peer_id = protocol principal (who sent this, cryptographically), actor_id = authority principal (on whose authority this capability is requested) -- distinct today, may be related by a FUTURE policy, never automatically equated by this mission.
destination_identity_semantics: No new destination_peer_id field was introduced. destination_node_id already provides the equivalent invariant this mission's Section 9 asked about: it is already part of canonical_request_fields()'s signed content (added in the original message-integrity mission) and already checked by both server scripts' pre-existing 'unknown node' guard (request.destination_node_id != node_id -> CAP_FAILED). Adding a duplicate destination_peer_id concept for the same already-solved invariant was judged unnecessary and was not built.

PEER IDENTITY resolution + peer/relationship binding check (NEW, evaluated strictly AFTER integrity succeeds so an unverified peer claim can never influence anything)

resulting_capability_claim.claim: LOCAL_PEER_IDENTITY_RELATIONSHIP_BINDING_PROVEN -- ForgeWorld can create a durable protocol-level peer identity, bind it to a proven local pairing relationship, integrity-bind that identity claim to governed requests, revoke it, preserve it (and its binding) across a real process restart, and enforce identity/relationship consistency (a valid peer under the wrong relationship, an unknown peer, a revoked peer, or a tampered peer claim all fail closed with zero execution) strictly before replay, authority, and capability execution -- without ever conflating peer identity with human identity, device ownership, authority, or any secret material.
